h: A Few Tricks for Your Manchester Night
p: Deansgate is a long road, and it's easy to underestimate how far it stretches, so it's worth figuring out where you're heading before you set off. Manchester's Metrolink trams run through the city centre, with stops such as Deansgate-Castlefield and St Peter's Square handy for this part of town, and Deansgate railway station sits at the southern end.

Spinningfields, just off Deansgate, is a modern business district packed with bars and restaurants, a good bet for pre-game drinks or dinner. For something a little more historic, Manchester Cathedral at the northern end of Deansgate is a beautiful medieval building in the middle of the busy city. The National Football Museum at Cathedral Gardens is another popular stop, especially for anyone in town for a match.

For the bowling itself, a few pointers. Go for a ball you can swing comfortably rather than the heaviest. Aim for the arrows on the lane rather than the pins at the end, as it's easier to hit a closer target, and follow through towards it. Mix up beginners and confident bowlers across teams for a fairer contest.

Planning a big group outing? Book well ahead, especially around Christmas party season, and agree a budget for food and drinks so there are no awkward conversations when the bill comes. Get there a few minutes early to sort shoes and a round before your start time.
